label: Grok Imagine 2.0 image generation and reference-driven editing

prompt_contract.style: prose description of one still frame
notes: A rendering style left unstated is filled by a surface default rather than inherited from the references.
A reference supplies likeness and drawing style; it does not supply the geometry of the frame, so scale, angle, and screen position stay in the text.

frame_control.resolution_parameter: width and height together, or the resolution preset with reference images
notes: The surface accepts a fixed set of width and height pairs and rejects a pair outside it.
The resolution preset (1K or 2K) is accepted only with reference images and takes the aspect from the input; it is exclusive with width and height.
A 2K pair carries about four times the pixels of its 1K counterpart, which is what decides how many features one reference can hold legibly.

input_modes.limits: at most three references in one request
input_modes.media_supplies: character likeness, wardrobe, drawing style, and the appearance of a room already established
input_modes.text_must_establish: camera position, shot scale, screen direction, pose, action, light direction, and every permanent feature that must appear in this frame

anti_patterns: A featureless base-body image submitted as a reference is rejected by the surface rather than treated as a neutral body.
Naming only some of the characters that a reference shows lets the unnamed one enter the frame uninvited.
A shot given a reference that carries a character will show that character. A frame that must not show him is written without a reference that carries him.
A wardrobe zone the frame will show and the text does not name is filled by a surface default, so a character with bare legs acquires trousers.

constraints.geometry: one of the listed width and height pairs, or a resolution preset with reference images
constraints.seed: unsupported: the service refuses the seed parameter for this model (Unsupported use of 'seed' parameter), so a composition cannot be reproduced or varied one word at a time
